capability.summary: Send one fixed preflight-style OPTIONS request and report selected CORS response headers
capability.description: Normalizes a scheme-less target to HTTPS, sends an OPTIONS request with a fixed example Origin and requested GET method, then returns the HTTP status plus any of five recognized Access-Control response headers. `cors_enabled` only indicates that at least one such header was present.
capability.problem_space: Single-endpoint observation of selected CORS response headers for one fixed Origin/GET probe; not comprehensive CORS policy validation, browser enforcement simulation, vulnerability certification, or file inspection.

env_requirements: network access to the target URL
constraint.io_signature: Input: one required HTTP(S) URL or scheme-less host/path string; output: JSON with normalized URL, response status, coarse header-presence boolean, and selected CORS headers, or a request error.
accepted_inputs: an absolute http:// or https:// URL
a scheme-less host or host/path string that should be requested over https://
constraint.output_shape: Successful HTTP exchange: {status: "success", tool: "requests", url: string, status_code: integer, cors_enabled: boolean, cors_headers: object}; cors_headers contains only present Access-Control-Allow-Origin, -Methods, -Headers, -Credentials, and Access-Control-Max-Age values, and cors_enabled is bool(cors_headers). Request failure: {status: "error", tool: "requests", url: string, message: string} and exit 1. Missing argument prints usage to stderr and exits 1 without JSON. HTTP error status codes still produce status="success" because raise_for_status is not called.
limitations: uses fixed `Origin: https://example.com` and `Access-Control-Request-Method: GET` headers with no caller customization
treats the presence of any selected CORS header as cors_enabled and does not judge policy correctness, credential safety, origin reflection, or browser exploitability
performs only one OPTIONS request with a 20-second Requests timeout; redirects and other Requests defaults are not exposed
scheme-less input is always prefixed with https:// and malformed URLs are reported only through the request exception

output_contract.description: JSON report of one fixed OPTIONS probe: normalized URL, HTTP status, selected CORS headers and their coarse presence flag, or a request error.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: inspect selected CORS headers returned by an endpoint
send a fixed GET preflight-style OPTIONS probe
negative_intents: prove that a CORS policy is secure or exploitable
test arbitrary origins, methods, headers, or credential scenarios
inspect HTTP security headers unrelated to CORS
